absent: Reclaim threshold evaluation and page selection policy beyond the high watermark check.
EPC allocation and free paths including reclaim tracking transitions and free list discipline.
Native enclave driver initialization and its failure modes.
Provision device operations and security version lock usage.
NUMA target mapping, fallback policy details, and free page counter updates.
Hardware fault encoding and all privileged instruction error codes.
Usage count increment failure conditions and concurrency rules.
CPU topology discovery beyond the identifier tables shown.

findings.text: A global table holds enclave page cache section descriptors with a companion count of populated entries and a background thread handle. A free page counter and a NUMA presence mask plus per node records track capacity distribution.
An EPC page record carries its owning section index, status flags, a poison marker, an owner reference for the enclave page using it, and list linkage for dirty, free or poison queues.
A NUMA node record holds a free page queue, a poison page queue, accumulated byte size, and a spin lock guarding queue membership and poison transitions.
An EPC section record holds a physical base, a mapped virtual base, an array of page records, and a back pointer to its NUMA node record.
A virtual EPC instance holds an indexed collection of assigned EPC pages and a mutex serializing fault handling and teardown.
A global reclaimer spin lock exists alongside per node spin locks that protect movement between free and poison queues and poison marking. A separate mutex guards security version state.
Each virtual EPC mutex must be held during fault resolution. A global zombie mutex guards a shared list of deferred control pages across release operations.
Maximum EPC sections is 8. Extend granularity is 256 bytes. Reclaim scan batch is 16 with low and high watermarks 32 and 64.
Reclaimer tracked marker is bit 0 and free marker is bit 1 of page flags.
Initialization token size for the virtual launch path is 304 bytes.

Module initialization requires the SGX feature, builds the page cache, starts the background thread, registers a provision device, then attempts native and virtual drivers, succeeding if either succeeds and unwinding mappings and the thread on failure.

Physical address membership can be queried and translated to a page record. Memory failure handling signals the task on synchronous consumption, marks poison once, and moves free pages to the poison queue while unmarking reclaimable busy pages for later cleanup on free.

Sanitization drains a caller local dirty queue, diverting poisoned entries to the node poison queue under the node lock, returning cleaned pages to the allocator and retaining still dirty ones for a later pass, reporting how many remain.

The background thread first performs two cleaning passes to cover pages blocked by children, warns if residue remains, then sleeps until stop or high watermark pressure and invokes reclamation. Startup spawns this thread and records its handle.

Cache setup allocates per node records, enumerates firmware sections until an invalid type, derives base and size metrics from identifier leaves, maps each section and creates its page records on a global dirty list, binds it to an online NUMA node with fallback, initializes per node state once, and fails if no section was usable.

Per node size exposes total EPC bytes. A grouped attribute under a short architecture name stays invisible while no NUMA node is initialized, becoming visible after first use of a node, with update failures logged. A build without node sysfs compiles the visibility refresh to an empty operation.

Two misc devices are exposed, one for provisioning and one for virtual EPC, each with dynamic minor allocation and matching short names. The virtual device supports open, ioctl, release and mapping operations.

Mapping requires shared semantics and installs fault operations with device mapping flags that prevent dumping and copying on fork. Faults serialize on the instance mutex, reuse an existing assignment or allocate and index a new page and insert its frame, returning a retry signal when busy under retryable faults and a bus error otherwise.

Release first frees child pages, then retries remaining entries which are control pages, erasing index slots as it goes. Unfreeable control pages join a local list that is reconciled with a global zombie list under its mutex, attempting to retire old zombies before splicing survivors, then destroys the index and drops a usage reference.

An ioctl with zero argument walks all virtual assignments attempting unconditional removal, counting control pages still blocked by children for userspace retry and failing busy on concurrent enclave activity or protection faults, while rejecting nonzero arguments and unknown commands.

Guest creation and initialization entry points validate user pointers for control, signature and token buffers, execute privileged operations with user access enabled, and translate hardware faults into trap numbers with distinct errors for invalid pointers versus faults. When launch control is available the caller supplied key hash is refreshed with preemption disabled around the launch call.

Checking poison without the node lock is intentionally racy but safe, only causing a redundant removal attempt. Persistent removal failures leak the page and may render the facility unusable. Concurrent execution inside an enclave or parallel removal across instances can induce busy failures that callers must retry.

The logical to physical identifier table starts fully invalid and becomes read only after init. Per domain bitmaps track physical identifiers and are also read only after init. Diagnostic output uses a short topology prefix.

An inter processor callback is defined as a no operation. Virtual EPC setup without virtualization support reports absence, while the full variant requires the virtualization feature, initializes zombie state and registers its device.
Shared header defines an include guard and a short log prefix for diagnostics.
